sources_considered.why: Representative April 2026 poll on views of Sam Altman. It is about Altman, not OpenAI, so context only.
Morning Consult poll from May 2026 on trust in AI company CEOs in general. Not OpenAI-specific, so context only.
Reports OpenAI's Q2 2026 business results from the WSJ. Context on business health.
Poll of young adults on AI leaders. Narrow population, and not read in full.

receipt.public_excerpt: Views among the rest were more negative than positive, with 28% unfavorable and 18% favorable.

evidence_items.explanation: Views of Altman lean negative, but most adults are unfamiliar or neutral. This measures favorability of one person, not trust in OpenAI, so it cannot settle the claim.

receipt.public_excerpt: AI company CEOs are trusted ‘a lot’ by just 13%, with 34% saying ‘not at all.’

evidence_items.explanation: Trust in AI company CEOs as a group is low, but about a third say 'not at all', not nearly everyone. It does not single out OpenAI.

evidence_items.publisher: Outlook Business (citing The Wall Street Journal)

receipt.public_excerpt: OpenAI told investors that its revenue increased 18% sequentially to $6.7 billion in the three months ended June, compared with $5.7 billion in the first quarter.

evidence_items.explanation: Revenue was still growing, though more slowly than investors hoped. The report blames competition and pricing, not distrust, so it does not test the causal link.

unresolved_gaps: No representative 2026 poll found that measures trust in OpenAI as a company.
No evidence found linking distrust of OpenAI to lost customers, retention, or revenue.
Available polls cover Altman or AI CEOs in general, not OpenAI.
